mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 5% YoY signals inflationary pressures that lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 5% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson's r < -0.1) over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson's r < -0.2) over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand environment, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson's r < -0.1) over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% YoY signals a strong supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO YoY > 2% does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson's r > 0.1) over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and increasing Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson's r < -0.1) over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in one month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or PAYEMS decrease > 100,000 does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson's r < -0.2) over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand environment, which leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson's r > 0.1) over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals an easing monetary cycle, which reduces borrowing costs and boosts corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson's r > 0.1) over a 5-year period.
